chunks: What Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, who said:

Some of our companions wrote to Abi al-Hasan عليه السلام: It has been narrated from your forefathers about the foot, the two feet, the four, the qamah, the two qamahs, your like-shadow, the cubit, and the two cubits.

So he عليه السلام wrote: Neither the foot nor the two feet. When the sun declines, the time of Zuhr has entered, and before it there is a supererogatory prayer, which is eight rakʿahs; if you wish, you may lengthen it, and if you wish, you may shorten it. Then pray Zuhr. When you finish, there is between Zuhr and ʿAsr a supererogatory prayer, which is eight rakʿahs; if you wish, you may lengthen it, and if you wish, you may shorten it. Then pray ʿAsr, because he only negated the foot and the two feet so that it should not be thought that nothing besides that is permissible, since what has been reported regarding that was reported in the sense of what is more excellent, not as an obligation. This clarifies what we have said.

key_terms.الْأَفْضَلِ: that which is more excellent or preferable in practice
key_terms.زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ: the sun declined from the meridian, marking the beginning of Zuhr time
key_terms.سُبْحَةٌ: a supererogatory prayer performed in addition to the obligatory prayer
key_terms.وَقْتُ الظُّهْرِ: the appointed time of the Zuhr prayer

ai.seo_question: When does the time of Zuhr begin, and are shadow measurements like a foot or two feet obligatory?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the time of Zuhr begins as soon as the sun declines from its zenith, without restricting its start to measurements such as a foot or two feet of shadow. It also clarifies that such reported measurements refer to what is more excellent or preferable, not to an obligatory condition, while mentioning the recommended supererogatory prayers before Zuhr and between Zuhr and ʿAsr.
